codes.invalid_argument: An argument the tool does not declare, a value of the wrong type, a missing required argument, or a combination the tool refuses, such as `headerScan` together with `headerRow`, or a `cursor` together with `sheetName` or `range`. The message names the conflict. For an undeclared or mistyped argument the recovery lists the arguments the tool accepts.
codes.invalid_range: `range` is not a valid A1 range. Use a form such as `B2:D40`, `B:D` or `2:40`.
codes.range_outside_used_range: `range` lies outside the sheet's used range. The recovery names the used range.
codes.invalid_cursor: `cursor` is not a token that a previous `read_sheet` answer returned, for example because it was cut short or edited. Read again without a cursor.
codes.stale_cursor: The file changed between two pages of the same read. Start again without a cursor.
codes.invalid_pattern: `find_in_sheet` refused a `regex` query: it is longer than 256 characters, uses a Unicode property escape (`\p{…}`), or is not a valid JavaScript regular expression.
codes.resource_limit: The request would exceed a fixed budget: too many groups or cells for `aggregate_sheet`, or a regex search that timed out or found the queue full. See [Limits](/docs/excel-mcp/limits).

codes.path_outside_root: `filePath` resolves outside the folder the server was started with. Paths are relative to that folder, and `..` cannot leave it.
codes.file_not_found: No file exists at `filePath`. Call `list_workbooks` for the paths that do.
codes.not_a_file: `filePath` names a directory or another entry that is not a regular file.
codes.file_too_large: The file or its metadata exceeds a resource bound: 50 MB for a workbook; for a CSV, 16 MB, 16,384 fields in one record or 2,000,000 cells. Rich metadata also has bounded record, field and value counts.
codes.file_changed: The file was modified while it was being read. Retry the call.
codes.unsupported_platform: The native package that gives the server safe file access is missing for this operating system and CPU. Reinstall on a supported platform.

codes.not_a_workbook: The bytes are not a workbook: not a zip archive at all, or a zip with no workbook part or no worksheet inside, such as a `.docx` renamed to `.xlsx`.
codes.encrypted_workbook: The file is password-protected or saved in the legacy binary `.xls` format. Save an unprotected `.xlsx` copy.
codes.corrupt_workbook: The file is a damaged workbook: a zip archive that cannot be indexed, a part that fails its CRC-32 check or whose local header disagrees with the central directory, or a part that is not well-formed XML or valid UTF-8 or that breaks a SpreadsheetML rule, including an invalid referenced rich-value index or relationship chain. A damaged sheet is refused only by the calls that read it, `describe_workbook` included. The message names the part and the fault. For a CSV: a quote inside an unquoted field, text after a closing quote, or a quote that never closes; the message names the fault and its line, and the file is never repaired.
codes.undecodable_text: A CSV cannot be decoded as text: it is not valid UTF-8 and has no byte-order mark, it is not valid text in the `encoding` passed, it contains NUL bytes near its start, which means a binary file or UTF-16 without a byte-order mark, or it starts with a UTF-32 byte-order mark. Pass the known source encoding from the tool’s closed encoding list.
codes.ambiguous_delimiter: Two delimiters fit the first 20 lines of a CSV equally well. Pass `delimiter`.
codes.numeric_overflow: A cell or a comparison value holds a number outside the finite range, such as `Infinity`.
codes.unsupported_for_format: The file's format cannot carry what was asked for, such as `get_tables` or `headerScan` on a CSV. `describe_workbook` lists what each file supports in its `capabilities` block.
codes.unsupported_object_kind: `get_images` was asked for charts, pivot tables or sparklines. Charts belong to `get_charts`; pivot tables and sparklines are unread in every format, so the server refuses rather than answer with an empty list. Selecting a table with unsupported header/totals row counts also fails explicitly; inspect it with range instead.

codes.unknown_sheet: No sheet has that name. Names are case-sensitive; the recovery lists the sheets that exist.
codes.ambiguous_sheet: Two sheets have names that are the same after Unicode normalization, so neither can be addressed. Rename one in the workbook.
codes.empty_sheet: The sheet has no stored values, or the selected table has no data rows after excluding its header and totals.
codes.chart_sheet: The sheet is a chart sheet: it holds a chart, not a cell grid. Call `get_charts`.
codes.unknown_column: A column named in `groupBy`, `metrics` or `where` is neither a header in the range nor an A1 letter. The recovery lists the named columns.
codes.ambiguous_column: A column reference matches more than one column: two columns share the header text, or the text is both a header and another column's letter. Address the column by letter.
codes.unknown_header_row: `headerScan` found no row that qualifies as a header. Pass `headerRow`, or `headerRow: 0` to read without headers.
codes.ambiguous_header_row: `headerScan` found more than one row that qualifies as a header, or more than one Excel Table declares one. The recovery quotes the candidate rows; pass `headerRow`.
codes.unknown_table: No declared table matches the requested name in the workbook or selected sheet. Call get_tables on the relevant worksheet.
codes.ambiguous_table: More than one table name matches after Unicode folding. Pass sheetName to restrict the lookup, or repair duplicate names.

codes.internal_error: A defect in the server, not in your file or your call. This is the one code with no `recovery`, because there is no next call that fixes it. The detail is written to the server's stderr.

keys.maxFileBytes: Largest `.xlsx` or `.xlsm` file the server opens
keys.maxCsvCells: Most cells a CSV may hold
keys.maxCsvColumns: Most fields one CSV record may hold
keys.csvNulScanBytes: Bytes at the start of a CSV checked for NUL bytes, which mark a binary file
keys.csvSniffBytes: Bytes of a CSV read to detect the delimiter
keys.csvSniffLines: Lines of a CSV compared to detect the delimiter
keys.documentCacheSize: Parsed files kept in memory between calls
keys.maxListScan: Directory entries `list_workbooks` walks before it reports `scanTruncated`

keys.maxPayloadBytes: Largest serialized answer; a longer one is cut short and continues through `nextCursor`
keys.maxStringChars: Longest text, in characters, returned for one cell or one formula
keys.guidanceRowThreshold: Rows above which `describe_workbook` and `read_sheet` suggest `aggregate_sheet` or `find_in_sheet` instead of paging

keys.maxAggregateGroups: Distinct groups one `aggregate_sheet` scan may form before it is refused with `resource_limit`
keys.maxAggregateMetricStates: Metric states retained across primary groups, pivots and grouping sets before `resource_limit`
keys.maxAggregateSamples: Exact percentile samples retained across all groups and grouping sets before `resource_limit`
keys.maxAggregateDistinctValues: Distinct metric values retained across all groups and grouping sets before `resource_limit`
keys.maxGroupingSets: Additional grouping sets in one `aggregate_sheet` call
keys.maxGroupBins: Explicit numeric boundaries in one grouping specification
keys.maxPivotCells: Metric cells in the complete dense row-key by pivot-key result before allocation
keys.maxAggregateCellVisits: Cells one `aggregate_sheet` call may read before it is refused with `resource_limit`
keys.maxErrorCodes: Named native-error code buckets in one aggregate result; further codes are counted in other
keys.maxErrorExamples: Example source addresses retained per native-error bucket
keys.maxErrorCodeChars: Maximum named native-error code length; longer codes are counted in other
keys.maxColumnSpecs: Shared column specifications accepted by profile_sheet, read_sheet, find_in_sheet and aggregate_sheet
keys.maxCursorChars: Characters in a `read_sheet` cursor, which carries the call's column specifications; a page whose next cursor would be longer is refused
keys.headerScanRows: Rows at the top of the range that `headerScan` examines

keys.maxProfileRowsDefault: Data rows sampled by profile_sheet when maxRows is omitted
keys.maxProfileColumnsDefault: Columns profiled when maxColumns is omitted
keys.maxProfileCells: Cells in one rectangular profile sample; a prefix is returned with omitted rows counted
keys.maxProfileDistinct: Distinct values retained per profiled column; larger cardinalities are lower bounds and topValuesComplete is false

keys.maxTablesPerSheet: Excel Tables `get_tables` reports for one sheet
keys.maxChartPointsDefault: Cached series points `get_charts` returns per series when `maxPoints` is omitted
keys.maxChartPointsPerResponse: Cached series points one `get_charts` answer may return across every series
keys.maxSeriesPerChart: Series one chart may declare before further series are dropped
keys.maxRangesPerRule: Ranges reported for one validation or conditional-format rule before `rangesTruncated`

hidden.catalogTtlMs: a cache hint on the `tools/list` answer, not a limit on a call
